en: The Triplet on the Visible (Sanidassanattika) and the Couple on with Rapture (Sappītikaduka)
Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable, non-reactive, and accompanied by rapture, there arises a state that is neither non-demonstrable nor non-reactive and is not accompanied by rapture,

by way of root condition. Dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable, non-reactive, and accompanied by rapture, there arises a state that is neither non-demonstrable nor with-reactive and is not accompanied by rapture,
by way of root condition …pe… dependent on a state that is non-demonstrable, non-reactive, and accompanied by rapture.

Dependent on states that are non-indicative, with resistance, and without zest, and states that are non-indicative, without resistance, and without zest, [other] states arise by way of root condition.
(Abbreviated. Six in the case of root; three in the case of object... [and so on] ... six in the case of non-disappearance.
Dependent on a state that is non-indicative, without resistance, and without zest, there arises a state that is non-indicative, with resistance, and without zest... [and so on].

A state arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a non-demonstrable, non-reactive, and joyless state, there arises a state that is neither non-demonstrable-and-reactive nor joyless by way of root condition.

Dependent on a non-demonstrable, non-reactive, and joyless state, there arise states that are both neither non-demonstrable-and-reactive nor joyless and neither non-demonstrable-and-reactive nor joyless.
They arise by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. Under the root condition there are three; ... pe ... under the non-disappearance condition there are three.
